newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures end week on lacklustre note.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures end week on lacklustre note.

text.p: Ending the week on a lacklustre note, German Bunds and futures were expected to kick off next week's activity in a similarly dull fashion, caught in sideways trading at least early in the week.
Although dealers said the market possessed a good fundamental base to push higher, a lack of impetus from the U.S. kept the market mostly range-bound this afternoon.

By 1512 GMT June Bund futures, traded in Frankfurt, were trading down 11 basis points at 100.83 while the June Bobl futures contract was up two basis points at 104.75. "Based on the price data, the session was dull," a dealer said.
But dealers said the 40 basis point price range in the DTB futures contract masked more interesting activity in the shorter end of the market where dealers said they saw considerable demand.
"There was quite a bit of interest in the short end in the cash market and there was interest in the Bobl too," a dealer said, explaining a lot of the business was seen coming from overseas.
Another dealer added that it appeared U.S. investors were parking funds at the short end of the German yield curve, nervous about another possible U.S. rate hike.
Next week dealers said German March M3 money supply growth numbers, expected from Monday, could only surprise the market in a negative fashion.

As several Bundesbank officials have already said there would be no scope for a German rate cut in the near-term, even a much lower M3 number is not seen prompting the Bundesbank into easing rates again, dealers said. On the other hand a headline figure much higher than average 8.3 percent rate expected by dealers could only hurt the market by possibly sending signals that the central bank's next step would be a rate hike.
